record.paper_title: Open problems in Euclidean Ramsey Theory
record.original_question: For positive real numbers a and b, a degenerate triangle with side lengths a, b, and a+b is a collinear three-point configuration whose two smaller consecutive distances are a and b. It is known that, for every dimension n, Euclidean n-space E^n can be colored with 16 colors so that no monochromatic copy of any such degenerate triangle occurs. Can the constant 16 be reduced, and in particular is there a universal number r < 16, possibly r = 2, with the same avoidance property?

evidence.quote: E^n can be 16-colored to prevent the degenerate (a,b,a+b) triangle
Conjecture 4 The number 16 above can be reduced.

artifact.self_contained_problem: For positive real numbers $a$ and $b$, call the ordered triple of collinear points $\{P_1,P_2,P_3\}\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ a degenerate $(a,b,a+b)$-triangle if, after suitable ordering along the line, the consecutive distances are $|P_1P_2|=a$ and $|P_2P_3|=b$ (so that $|P_1P_3|=a+b$). A coloring $\chi:\mathbb{R}^n\to C$ is said to avoid degenerate triangles if there is no choice of positive reals $a,b$ and no degenerate $(a,b,a+b)$-triangle whose three points all receive the same color under $\chi$.\n\nIt is known that for every positive integer $n$ there exists a coloring of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $16$ colors that avoids all degenerate triangles in the above sense. Determine whether the constant $16$ can be reduced: that is, find the smallest positive integer $r$ such that for every $n$ there exists a coloring of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $r$ colors avoiding every degenerate $(a,b,a+b)$-triangle. In particular, decide whether $r=2$ suffices.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of reducing the number 16 in this avoidance result for degenerate (a,b,a+b)-triangles in Euclidean Ramsey theory appears to remain open; references such as Graham's survey on Euclidean Ramsey theory present it as a conjecture, and no resolution was found in the search.

status_evidence.title: Euclidean Ramsey Theory (Graham survey)
status_evidence.snippet: E^n can be 16-colored so as to prevent monochromatic degenerate (a,b,a+b) triangles; whether 16 can be reduced is stated as an open conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The bound 16 for avoiding degenerate (a,b,a+b)-triangles is recorded in the standard survey, with the question of reducing it left open.
